sample_unit: patients (preoperative medical records of primary unilateral TKA)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of covered checklist items and safety classification across three repeated LLM runs
links.effect: Pairwise Jaccard similarity 0.813 to 0.823; 126 of 180 (70.0%) CL-MNCIs covered in all three runs; safety agreement 87.5 to 95.8%.
links.quote: Of 180 CL-MNCIs, 126 (70.0%) were covered in all three runs, and case-level agreement in safety classification ranged from 87.5 to 95.8%.

links.outcome: Clinically inaccurate or unsafe LLM outputs identified by expert review of generated items
links.effect: Of 716 generated items, 12 safety events occurred across 9 cases; 39 items had insufficient record support and 50 were redundant.
links.quote: The LLM generated 716 items, including 12 safety events across 9 cases, 483 items matching CL-MNCIs, 132 record-supported supplementary items, 50 redundant items, and 39 items with insufficient record support.

unlisted_practices: Expert-panel-developed case-level minimum necessary communication items as reference standard for LLM cost-communication preparation
Limiting LLM use to clinician-reviewed communication preparation rather than direct patient cost disclosure

screen.reason: The study is an offline empirical evaluation assessing LLM performance in identifying preoperative cost-communication cues and generating preparation checklists from real patient records, including safety event analysis, but it does not compare outcomes with versus without an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
